newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end strong, feeders set new highs.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end strong, feeders set new highs.

text.p: CME live cattle futures finished under best levels but closed strong on fundamental and technical support and feeder cattle set new contract highs in March and April before ending under best levels.

Live cattle ran up to 5-week highs in active early trade before closing 0.800 to 0.275 higher. December paced the advance at 67.525 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.900 to 0.300 higher with January up 0.900 at 67.775 cents. March posted a new high of 67.450 and May a new high of 67.250 cents.
Fund demand touched off early buy stops in live cattle before profit taking pared gains late, traders said.

Support from strong fundamentals provided underlying support and fund buying took live cattle futures up to highs. Futures showed a breakout to the upside on charts with buy stops touched off above a trend line and above last week's highs, they said.
Very current feedlot conditions with some December cattle being pulled ahead provided the bulk of fundamental strength. The large discount of futures to cash also prompted short covering, they said.
"(Futures's) six cent discount to cash is too much," said Jim Clarkson, analyst for A and A Inc.
E.D.&F. Man, Cargill Investor Services, Dean Witter, Refco and R.J. O'Brien were buyers. Refco also spread long February/short December, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, there was short covering in December calls with volatility steady to firm. Commercials were hedging in February and April, pit sources added.

Feeder cattle futures followed the lead of live cattle to set new contract highs in the spring months. Good demand for replacement feeders and a higher index added to the spillover strength which also offset higher corn futures. Buy stops added to the midsession rally, they said.
"Cash feeders have been shown all last week and are expected to be strong this week," Clarkson said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.37 to $63.85 per cwt, the highest level since October 3.

Fimat Futures USA bought while LFG sold late. ADM Investor Services and LIT division of First Options spread long March/short November. Cargill Investor Services bought October live cattle while selling May feeders, pit sources said.
